title: Vulnerability signal correlation and patch velocity (June 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc collects correlated signals across our scanners, maps them to owners and patch SLAs, and documents gaps in evidence automation for SIEM exports. The goal is to create a single remediation feed we can push into the RedOps dashboard and the SIEM ingest pipeline with minimal manual work.

Background and motivation:
- We currently run three primary vulnerability signals: container/static image scans (Trivy), dependency SCA (Dependabot + Snyk results forwarded from CI), and infra/OS scans (Nessus scheduled on hosts).
- These scanners produce overlapping but inconsistent findings (same CVE flagged on image layer vs. package manifest vs. host package). Triaging duplicates costs ~20% of triage time.
- Patch velocity (time from detection to deployed fix) varies by class: infra/host patches average 9 days, container base image updates average 16 days, and library dep patches average 28 days (long tail due to app risk review and test flakiness). We want to reduce med/high CVE MTTR to <=14 days.

High-level proposal:
1) Signal correlation layer: lightweight matching rules to join scanner hits into a single canonical finding. Fields used: canonical CPE/CVSS/CVE id, artifact type (image/host/library), first_seen timestamps, evidence list (scanner:id:output_path), and suggested remediation (upgrade/downgrade/remove).
2) Owner assignment heuristics: map artifact types to teams and owners via CODEOWNERS-like rules pulled from repo manifests and inventory. Fallback: platform-sre for infra hosts; infra-team for base images; owning-service for application dependencies.
3) SLA tiers: Critical (CVE-1/CVSS>=9 or active exploit) = 72 hours; High (CVSS 7-8.9) = 14 days; Medium (CVSS 4-6.9) = 60 days; Low = discretionary. These align with legal/compliance inputs for enterprise customers.
4) Evidence automation and SIEM export: standardized evidence JSON per finding (flat keys) that maps to our SIEM schema for ingestion into Splunk/Chronicle.

Scanner outputs observed (summary of latest run, 2026-06-24):
- Trivy (container scan): 112 total findings; 8 high, 24 medium. Notable: CVE-2026-2134 (glibc) flagged in multiple base images; prioritized for base-image rebuild.
- Snyk/Dependabot (SCA): 187 findings across 42 repos; 5 high, 67 medium. Many medium findings are transitive deps in frontend bundles.
- Nessus (host scan): 54 findings; 3 high (SSH-related CVE backports on legacy hosts), 16 medium. One host shows outdated kernel requiring scheduled maintenance.
- Runtime agent signals (Falco rules): 6 alerts in last 7d; 2 correlated to same container image flagged by Trivy (suspicious process spawn pattern).

Example canonical finding (format we want to emit):
- id: VULN-2026-06-24-000137
- cve: CVE-2026-2134
- cvss: 8.7
- canonical_cpe: cpe:2.3:a:gnu:glibc:2.34:*:*:*:*:*:*:*
- artifact_type: container_base_image
- image_digest: sha256:abcd...
- first_seen: 2026-06-24T03:12:00Z
- evidence: ["trivy:scan/abcd.json:layers/3", "docker_registry:tags:stable-2026-06-03"]
- suggested_fix: rebuild-base-image-with-glibc-2.35
- owner_hint: infra-images@redwood.com
- sla_tier: High
- status: assigned
(We will represent the above as a flat JSON when exporting to SIEM.)

Evidence automation gaps (current blockers):
- Trivy outputs are stored as blob JSON in GCS but there is no stable object key pattern. Need to enforce path format: gs://vuln-scans/{scanner}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{repo-or-image}/{scan-id}.json
- Dependabot webhook payloads are transient in GitHub; we need archival via our CI job that uploads normalized SCA reports to the vuln bucket.
- Nessus export automation exists but mapping between host_id and our inventory (CMDB) sometimes fails for hosts decommissioned mid-cycle. Add inventory reconciliation run prior to importing.
- Runtime signals currently in a separate ElastiSearch cluster; we need a transform lambda to append container image digest and canonical cve before join.

SIEM export schema (flat keys required by Splunk ingest):
- event_type: "vuln_finding"
- finding_id: string
- cve: string
- cvss: numeric (string type in export allowed)
- severity: string (Critical|High|Medium|Low)
- artifact_type: string
- resource_id: string (host_id or image_digest or repo_full_name)
- first_seen: ISO8601
- last_seen: ISO8601
- owners: comma-separated list
- sla_tier: string
- suggested_fix: string
- evidence_refs: semicolon-separated refs (scanner:name|path)
- ticket_link: string (Jira)

Remediation tracking (current open list, simplified):
- VULN-2026-06-137 (CVE-2026-2134) - owner: infra-images - action: base-image rebuild scheduled - due: 2026-07-01 - evidence: gs://vuln-scans/trivy/2026/06/images/abcd-20260624.json - notes: needs regression test in nightly image pipeline.
- VULN-2026-06-201 (CVE-2026-1987) - owner: payments-service - action: bump dependency stripe-sdk 2.x -> 2.3.1 - due: 2026-07-11 - blocker: failing integration tests in CI.
- VULN-2026-06-189 (host-kernel-legacy) - owner: infra-sre - action: schedule kernel update maintenance window - due: 2026-06-30 (delayed) - notes: awaiting change approval.

Patch SLA compliance dashboard ideas (what to surface):
- Count of open findings by SLA tier and owner team
- MTTR rolling 30/90 day for High and Critical
- Time-in-state distribution (new -> triage -> assigned -> fixed -> verified)
- Duplicate suppression rate (how many incoming scanner hits matched an existing canonical finding)
- Evidence completeness score (has at least 1 scanner output + at least 1 owner + ticket)

Operational runbook snippets (triage flow):
1) New canonical finding created by correlation job -> attempt auto-assign via owner hints. If owner unknown, assign to security-triage@redwood.com.
2) Create Jira ticket with template (auto-populate fields from canonical finding). Attach evidence JSON URL(s).
3) Auto-run repo-level test harness (if artifact is app dependency) to detect breaking changes; post result to Jira.
4) If no action within SLA windows, auto-escalate to oncall and send Slack escalation.

RBAC v2 and audit log implications:
- Only RBAC groups with "vuln:write" should be allowed to update canonical findings and mark them fixed. Read-only roles can add comments and append evidence.
- Audit logs must include: actor, action, finding_id, pre_state_snapshot, post_state_snapshot, timestamp. We need to ensure these fields are in the audit schema so we can meet PCI/ISO requirements for change evidence.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should we treat transitive frontend bundle vulnerabilities (large number of medium findings) as lower priority until we have a path to rebuild/shrink bundles? Proposal: de-prioritize non-exploitable transitive deps until security-research verifies exploitability. (Input from Product needed)
- Do we enforce image digest immutability in deregulated envs to improve matching? This will require changes to our registry retention policy.
- SLA exceptions: allow owners to request extension via Jira workflow; accept if documented and routed to security leadership for approval.

Next action items (owners):
- Priya: draft canonical finding JSON schema + example normalization lambda (due 2026-07-02)
- Daniel Kim: implement GCS path policy enforcement in nightly CI (due 2026-07-09)
- Aisha: add inventory reconciliation step before Nessus import (due 2026-07-05)
- Marcus: prototype SIEM export transformer for Splunk ingest (due 2026-07-12)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic — it's a strawman to reduce duplicate triage work and get us to a single remediation feed. Please mark up owner assignments and SLA tiers where your team disagrees.
- Refer to linked artifacts at top for existing playbooks and PRs.

Revision history:
